subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: Should cron overflow recovery automatically delete older quarantine archives after five retained files, or should the hardening stop at a bounded read/write failure until a different recovery contract is designed?
rationale: The cap prevents an availability failure, but automatic pruning changes the persistence and recoverability contract for quarantined user configuration; repository policy treats fallback and retained-state loss as a product decision rather than an implementation convenience.

options.title: Approve a rolling five-archive window
options.body: Accept automatic deletion of the oldest quarantine records after the fifth archive, with the retention behavior treated as the supported recovery contract.

options.title: Keep the cap fail-closed for now
options.body: Retain the bounded reader and oversized-entry rejection, but remove automatic archive pruning until a maintainer-approved recovery and retention design exists.

options.title: Specify another bounded recovery policy
options.body: Define an owner-supported byte, age, export, or doctor-mediated retention approach before merging archive rotation.

recommendation.title: Keep the cap fail-closed for now
recommendation.body: Retain the bounded reader and oversized-entry rejection, but remove automatic archive pruning until a maintainer-approved recovery and retention design exists.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current retention implementation and can incorporate the selected direction; current-main ownership could not be established from the supplied review material.
